# Outline and Contour Generation

## Overview
Outline and Contour Generation is a family of Illustrative and Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) techniques that extract and stylize edges to emphasize the form, boundaries, and topological structure of volumetric or geometric data [S1, S2, unofficial]. Unlike standard photorealistic rendering which relies on shading and lighting for depth cues, these methods explicitly generate line-based or stroke-based overlays to demarcate object boundaries, silhouettes, and internal features [S1, S2, unofficial]. This family is distinguished from its siblings by its focus on generating explicit contour lines (as opposed to surface highlights or pure silhouette detection) through various means: pixel-based gradient analysis, user-defined interactive selection, curvature-aware analytical conditions, or object-space mesh processing [787-object-contour-npr.md][1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md][5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md][7959-silhouette-rendering.md].

## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md)
Object Contour NPR generates view-dependent lines that demarcate areas where an object's surface turns away from the viewer, effectively emphasizing physical boundaries [787-object-contour-npr.md]. Unlike analytical methods that require explicit vector representations, this approach is pixel-based and relies on gradient estimation within the volume data [787-object-contour-npr.md]. It is distinguished from sibling methods like Lasso Contour Rendering by its specific use of geometry shaders to trace line-strips from particle primitives, and from Silhouette Rendering by its reliance on local gradient magnitude and orientation rather than just visibility occlusion [787-object-contour-npr.md]. See [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) for implementation details.

### [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md)
Lasso Contour Rendering is an interactive, pixel-based outline generation method that allows users to manually define regions of interest within a volume using a freehand "lasso" selection tool [1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md]. Unlike automatic contour methods that detect edges based on scalar field gradients, this approach relies on user intent to highlight specific structures. It is distinguished by its integration into a real-time rendering pipeline where the contour is rendered dynamically only when the user is actively drawing, leveraging offscreen render passes to composite the selection overlay [1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md]. See [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md) for implementation details.

### [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md)
Curvature-Controlled Style Contours is an analytical-style contour generation method that regulates contour thickness based on the normal curvature along the view direction to prevent uncontrolled variation in thickness caused by the difference between flat and fine structures [5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md]. Unlike standard dot-product contours which produce lines that are too thick on flat surfaces and too thin on fine structures, this method ensures roughly constant image-space thickness [5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md]. It builds on [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by introducing a curvature-aware threshold condition. See [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md) for implementation details.

### [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md)
Silhouette rendering is an object-space line rendering technique that extracts significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines) from geometry, assembles them into strokes, and applies hidden line removal and stylization to enhance the perception of form and context [7959-silhouette-rendering.md]. It is primarily used in medical visualization to indicate context objects (e.g., bones) or to discriminate object classes based on specific features, such as lymph nodes touching critical structures [7959-silhouette-rendering.md]. Unlike pixel-based contour methods, this approach is resolution-independent and vector-oriented, allowing for explicit analytical representation and transformation without aliasing [7959-silhouette-rendering.md]. It builds on the principles of [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md). See [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md) for implementation details.

### [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md)
Topological Landscape is a visualization technique that maps the topology of a scalar field onto a 3D terrain model to enhance the interpretability of contour relationships [8481-topological-landscape.md]. It builds on [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by converting abstract graph structures into an intuitive spatial representation where valleys indicate contour splits and peaks indicate contour merges [8481-topological-landscape.md]. Unlike [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) which renders lines directly on the volume, this method provides a meta-visualization of the data's structural hierarchy. See [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md) for implementation details.

### Image Space Outline Generation
- **Definition**: A pixel-based method to generate simple outlines by extracting edges from depth or normal maps, observing that depth differences are minimal between adjacent pixels of a single object and large between objects, and normals vary smoothly across a single surface but show discontinuity between surfaces [S1, unofficial].
- **Steps**: Extract edges from a depth map or normal map using an edge detection mechanism, such as the Sobel filter [S1, unofficial]. Combine detected depth and normal edges to yield perceptually significant silhouettes [S1, unofficial]. For further processing (e.g., modifying line qualities), calculate analytical curves from the detected edge map, as detected edges only exist as lists of pixels [S1, unofficial].
- **Comparison**: Depth edges reflect C0 discontinuities, while normal edges reflect C1 discontinuities; combining both yields all perceptually significant silhouettes [S1, unofficial].

### Ghosted Views with Contours
- **Steps**: Pre-segment the most interesting internal structures (e.g., small internal organs) [S2, unofficial]. Identify context information (e.g., the body) that obscures the interesting structures [S2, unofficial]. In areas of occlusion, reduce the visual representation of the context object to contours [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of using outlines to enhance visual perception in computer graphics has roots in early non-photorealistic rendering research. Hertzmann presented a survey of image space outline generation algorithms in [Her99], noting that pixel-based methods are generally faster and simpler to implement than analytical methods [S1, unofficial]. Schlechtweg and Raab described a flexible line model where the path is expressed using parametric curves, with style attributes (width, brightness) mapped to visual properties [S1, unofficial]. In the context of volume rendering, these techniques have been adapted to handle 3D scalar fields, with applications in medical visualization (e.g., CT-angiography, highlighting lymph nodes) and scientific visualization (e.g., hurricane moisture data) [S2, unofficial]. The field continues to evolve with interactive methods and curvature-aware analytical approaches to improve the perceptual quality of volumetric outlines [787-object-contour-npr.md][5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md].
